title.narrative: Increased capacity of national institutions to develop entrepreneurship programmes, including to provide services to MSEs, cooperatives and youth

description.narrative: A major challenge in The Gambia is the limited national capacity of the economies to generate decent employment for youth and foster the creation of sustainable enterprises. As a result, micro and small enterprises and their workers are trapped in the informal economy, which is characterized by poor working conditions, low quality employment, inadequate access to social protection, low productivity and revenues. This is due to macroeconomic instability and an unconducive business enabling environment that makes formalizing a business too costly and cumbersome. At the same time, the capacity of government to enforce business registration requirements is weak, and there are generally very few incentives and support schemes that would push enterprises to formalize. The implementation of the actions in this CPO will put particular emphasis on building the capacity of constituents to facilitate the formalisation of the informal sector, promote youth entrepreneurship while at the same time promote the development of partnerships and synergies both within the ILO and with UN agencies, the private sector and the civil society. The target young men and women entrepreneurs, both working and aspiring, will be equipped with entrepreneurial and business development skills, as well as a greater inspiration and change of mindset, which will enable them to establish and grow formal and sustainable businesses. A new training programme will be designed to assist potential and existing entrepreneurs in the formalisation process. The aim is to show them why and how to formalise a business in The Gambia. At the macro level, the CPO will contribute to improving the knowledge of constituents on the challenges of formalisation. It will also contribute to providing technical support for the formulation of a strategy and action plan for the transition to the formal economy for enterprises and workers.
